queries.hook: A mind that will not settle for twenty minutes, and the guilt that every minute not spent studying is a rupee wasted.
queries.diagnose: The untrained mind runs like the wind, replaying and imagining; left to itself it becomes its own enemy, and it turns every worry into a proof.
queries.steady: Praise and blame, success and failure, come and go; what is real in you cannot be taken by a result, and no honest effort is ever lost.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन । बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम् ॥
verse.line: A decided mind is single and focused. An undecided mind splits into endless branches.
verse.translation: Here, Arjuna, the resolute mind is one-pointed. But the thoughts of the irresolute are many-branched and endless.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield. Arjuna is paralyzed by doubt about whether to fight his own family. Krishna tells him that a mind that is settled and resolved stays single and focused. But an undecided mind splits into endless branches. He is telling Arjuna to commit fully to the action before him, and to let go of owning the outcome. This is the beginning of the yoga of action. It is a steadying voice in the middle of a crisis.
verse.for_you: You are trying to settle your mind for an exam, but it keeps splitting into endless branches. You open Instagram, then you feel guilty about the coaching fees, then you panic about the result. The guilt and the panic are the branches. They are not the exam itself.

verse.speaker: Nidagha
verse.sanskrit: इतश्चेतश्च सुव्यग्रं व्यर्थमेवाभिधावति । मनो दूरतरं याति ग्रामे कौलेयको यथा ॥
verse.line: The mind runs here and there for nothing, wandering far like a stray village dog.
verse.translation: The mind runs here and there, restless and pointless; it wanders far away, like a dog in a village.
verse.why: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.

prasang.title: Nidagha's lament
prasang.summary: Young Nidagha returns from pilgrimage disillusioned and pours out his heart to his teacher Ribhu: life is fleeting, the mind runs like a stray dog, craving gnaws every good quality, and mastering the mind is harder than drinking the ocean.
prasang.lesson: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.

verse.meaning: Nidagha, a young student, returns from a pilgrimage and tells his teacher Ribhu that his mind is restless and pointless. Ribhu tells him that the mind runs here and there, wandering far away, like a stray village dog. He names the wandering without trying to fix it immediately. He shows that simply seeing the mind for what it is, running after nothing, is the first step toward peace. The wandering is the problem, and the naming of it is the beginning of the cure.
verse.for_you: Yesterday's verse named the grip. Today you see the pattern underneath it. Your mind is not broken. It is just running after a result it cannot hold. When you open Instagram, it is the dog running after a scent it cannot catch. Let it run. You do not have to chase it.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
verse.sanskrit: न प्रहृष्येत्प्रियं प्राप्य नोद्विजेत्प्राप्य चाप्रियम् । स्थिरबुद्धिरसम्मूढो ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मणि स्थितः ॥
verse.line: Don't get carried away by good news or crushed by bad. Keep your understanding steady.
verse.translation: One should not rejoice on getting what is pleasant nor be troubled on getting what is unpleasant. Steady in understanding and undeluded, the knower of Brahman abides in Brahman.
verse.why: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how the wise live and work.
verse.sanskrit: यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः । समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥
verse.line: Content with what comes, beyond envy, steady in success and failure, you stay free even while working.
verse.translation: Content with whatever comes unasked, beyond the pairs of opposites, free from envy, the same in success and failure, even when acting he is not bound.
verse.why: Contentment and freedom from envy let you work without being bound.

prasang.title: How the great yogis live
prasang.summary: The wise act without selfish motive, content and dependent on nothing, free from envy, steady in success and failure.

prasang.title: Prahlada: effort and grace are not rivals
prasang.summary: After telling how Prahlada awakened, Vasishtha faces Rama's challenge: if everything comes by effort, wasn't Prahlada saved by Vishnu's grace? Vasishtha answers that Prahlada earned it himself, that the Self and Vishnu are not two, and that sometimes we wake by our own effort and sometimes by grace reached through devotion. Steady daily practice ripens the mind like a mango.
prasang.lesson: Grace and effort work together; keep practising daily, and let the mind ripen slowly.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha tells Rama that effort and grace are not rivals. A mango does not ripen because it is forced, but because it is tended to day after day. The mind becomes clear through steady practice and clear thinking. It ripens slowly, and the sweetness is not rushed.
verse.for_you: Your mind is restless, and the coaching fees feel like a weight. Try sitting with your books for one minute. Then five. Do not force focus. Let the mind ripen slowly, like a mango.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha tells Rama how to steer his own habits.
verse.sanskrit: समता सांत्वनेनाशु न द्रागिति शनेशनेः । पौरुषेणैव यत्नेन पालयेच्चित्तबालकम् ॥
verse.line: Raise your mind like a child: gently, patiently, little by little, never by force.
verse.translation: With evenness and gentle coaxing, not in a rush but little by little, by steady effort, look after the child that is your mind.
verse.why: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

prasang.title: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort
prasang.summary: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
prasang.lesson: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

He tells Rama not to grieve over what was never in his hands. Instead of forcing the mind, Vasishtha says to look after it like a child, with gentle coaxing and steady effort, little by little. What comes next in the story shows Rama that what people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort.
verse.for_you: You open Instagram again because the guilt of the coaching fees is loud. Today, try to look after that restlessness like a child. Hold the mind for one minute, then five. Let the result go.

story.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
story.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
story.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
story.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

anchor.speaker: Janaka
anchor.setting: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof after overhearing wandering sages, rethinks his life.
anchor.sanskrit: संपदश्च विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेच्चित्तेन संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा हन्त मन्ये महापदः ॥ आपदोऽपि विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेन्मनसि संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा मन्ये मनसि संपदः ॥
anchor.line: Good fortune the mind clutches becomes trouble. Trouble the mind accepts becomes a kind of fortune.
anchor.translation: All those dazzling fortunes, if the mind clings to them, are really great calamities in grand disguise. And all those varied misfortunes, if the mind accepts them, are really fortunes.
anchor.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
anchor.misuse: Accepting a hardship doesn't mean not fixing what can be fixed.

script: Your mind will not sit still for twenty minutes. You open Instagram. Then the two lakhs in coaching fees hit you. Then the panic starts. It feels like you are falling apart.
Arjuna is on a battlefield. He is paralyzed. He cannot see a single path forward. Krishna tells him that a mind that is settled stays single and focused. Krishna said:
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन, बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम्.
In plain words: A decided mind is single and focused. An undecided mind splits into endless branches.

What you are living with is a mind that splits into endless branches. One branch is the phone. Another is the money. Another is the fear of the result. This is easier said than done, because your brain is trying to solve everything at once. But you cannot hold all the branches. You can only hold one. The teaching is to choose one branch and stay there.
When the mind splits, do not fight the phone. Do not fight the guilt. Just name the one thing in front of you right now. The next chapter. The next question. That is the only branch to hold.
Can you hold just this one branch?

depth.life: You are staring at a textbook for an exam in three weeks, but your mind is already on Instagram. You feel guilty about the two lakhs you spent on coaching, and then you panic that this restlessness means you are wasting it. The guilt and the panic are the branches. The exam is just the tree.
depth.points: Krishna tells Arjuna that an undecided mind splits into endless branches. You are trying to control the result of the exam, so your mind cannot settle on the single task of studying. The branches are your thoughts, not the exam itself.
depth.practice: Set a timer for five minutes and read only one page, with your phone in another room. Do not check the time or the result.
depth.question: What is the single page you could read right now?
